# RAG Grounding Checklist: Ticket Knowledge Q&A (RAG)

**Purpose**: Validate that requirements covering grounding, anti-hallucination, and citation integrity for `POST /api/ai/ask` are complete, clear, consistent, and testable — not that the implementation works.
**Created**: 2026-09-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [architecture.md](../architecture.md), [rag-api-contract.md](../rag-api-contract.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## No-General-Knowledge / Answer-Only-From-Context

- [x] CHK001 Is the requirement that answers come only from retrieved ticket context specific enough to test — does it distinguish "no fallback to general knowledge" from "supplementing" retrieved content? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK002 Is the double-guardrail design (empty-retrieval short-circuit at architecture.md §5 step 4, plus a system-prompt instruction at step 5) documented as two independent, both-required controls, rather than implying either alone is sufficient? [Consistency, Architecture §5]
- [x] CHK003 Does a requirement exist for what happens when retrieval returns hits above threshold but the retrieved content still doesn't actually answer the specific question asked (as opposed to zero/low-similarity hits)? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: FR-016 + Edge Cases + SC-007 (spec.md); dedicated golden-set category (evaluation-strategy.md §1)

## No-Match / "No Relevant Tickets Found"

- [x] CHK004 Is the exact trigger condition for "no relevant tickets found" fully specified (zero hits OR all hits below threshold), with no ambiguity about a partial-hits case (e.g. 1 of 5 requested top-K above threshold)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, rag-api-contract.md §3]
- [x] CHK005 Is it explicitly required that the "no relevant tickets found" answer text is fixed/non-generated (not produced by the chat model), so this response itself cannot be a fabrication? [Completeness, rag-api-contract.md §3]
- [x] CHK006 Are the HTTP status code and response shape for the no-match case unambiguous and distinguished from an actual error response? [Consistency, rag-api-contract.md §3 vs §4]

## Citation Integrity

- [x] CHK007 Is "ticket IDs actually used to produce the answer" defined precisely enough to be testable — i.e., derived from retrieved-chunk metadata rather than parsed from the model's free-text output? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, Architecture §2 step 7]
- [x] CHK008 Is there a requirement covering the case where the model's generated text mentions a ticket ID that was not actually retrieved — must the response's `ticketIds` field still exclude it? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK009 Is there a requirement covering the case where retrieved chunks belong to conflicting tickets (differing resolutions for similar symptoms) — must all contributing ticket IDs be cited rather than one silently chosen? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK010 Can "every non-empty answer MUST include the ticket ID(s) actually used" be objectively verified without access to the model's internal reasoning (i.e., via the retrieval-set-vs-response-set comparison)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]

## Failure Handling Without Fabrication

- [x] CHK011 Is the required behavior on chat-model failure/timeout after successful retrieval distinct and unambiguous from both the grounded-answer and no-match response shapes (no accidental overlap in status code or body shape)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, rag-api-contract.md §4]
- [x] CHK012 Does a requirement/error-code exist for embedding-call or vector-store failure (retrieval-side failure), separate from generation-side failure? [Completeness, rag-api-contract.md §4]
- [x] CHK013 Is it specified that a failed generation must not return a partial answer (e.g. a truncated or half-formed response) rather than either a full answer or a clean error? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015]

## Single Retrieval → Generate Flow (No Agentic Actions)

- [x] CHK014 Is "single retrieval-then-generate step" precise enough to rule out multi-hop retrieval or retrieval retries within one request, or is that left ambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013] — Resolved: FR-013 now states "exactly one retrieval call and exactly one generation call ... no repeated/retried retrieval, no multi-step or multi-hop lookups"
- [x] CHK015 Is the requirement that the flow must not create/modify/delete tickets or send notifications testable independently of what the model is asked to do (i.e., verifiable by absence of mutating collaborators, not by trusting the model's compliance)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013, test-strategy.md §1]
- [x] CHK016 Are all categories of disallowed side effects enumerated (ticket mutation, notifications, "any other tool or side-effecting action"), or does the open-ended "any other" clause leave a gap in what must be tested? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013] — Resolved: FR-013 now requires the guarantee hold structurally (no reachable mutating/notification capability in the code path), not by enumerating an exhaustive list of forbidden actions — closes the open-ended-clause gap by making it a code-path property instead

## Configuration & Guardrail Tunability

- [x] CHK017 Is it unambiguous which specific config values (top-K, similarity threshold) affect grounding behavior, distinct from values that only affect performance/cost? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, rag-api-contract.md §5]
- [x] CHK018 Is there a requirement (or explicit non-requirement) for what counts as an acceptable default similarity threshold, or is "configurable" alone treated as sufficient without any documented starting rationale? [Gap, rag-api-contract.md §5]

## Traceability & Evaluation Alignment

- [x] CHK019 Do the golden-set "no-match" and "low-similarity" categories in evaluation-strategy.md map directly back to the two trigger conditions named in Spec §FR-006, with no third trigger condition left unevaluated? [Consistency, evaluation-strategy.md §1 vs Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK020 Is the manual grounding-check procedure (evaluation-strategy.md §3) specific enough to be repeatable by a different reviewer and reach the same pass/fail conclusion, or does it rely on undefined judgment calls? [Clarity, evaluation-strategy.md §3] — Resolved: §3 now requires pointing to a specific sentence per claim/citation (sentence-level, citation-necessity, reversal checks), each a per-item pass/fail instead of one subjective overall impression

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
